newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pandora, Kutubu combine on PNG gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pandora, Kutubu combine on PNG gas pipeline.

text.p: The Pandora offshore gas field project in the Gulf of Papua and the Kutubu onshore project have agreed to combine in planning a pipeline project to deliver natural gas from Papua New Guinea to Queensland, Pandora stakeholder Beach Petroleum NL said on Tuesday.

Beach chief executive Reg Nelson said in a statement the Pandora joint venture would contribute its extensive work to date developing the Pandora to Queensland pipeline while Kutubu operator Chevron Corp would contribute its work on the Kutubu to Queensland project.
Pandora is located in offshore permit PPL 82.

The two parties had agreed to combine their respective efforts into one, major gas pipeline project for the delivery of both onshore and offshore gas from PNG to Queensland, with Chevron taking over as project developer, he said.
Nelson told Reuters there was no guarantee at this stage the pipeline would be built but there was quiate a high probability.
There was no strict timetable but the participants would want planning to proceed as quickly as possible, he added.

The PPL 82 joint venture is headed by Canada's International Petroleum Corp with a 48.1890 percent stake, with other stakeholders Mobil Corp unit Ampolex Ltd 16.3636 percent, Command Petroleum Holdings NL 12.7273 percent, Beach 6.3636 percent and Oil Search Ltd and Secab Niugini Pty Ltd 5.0 percent each.

The arrangement with Chevron would ensure the broadest possible base of PNG gas would be accessible to the pipeline system, including both the Pandora and other potential offshore gas as well as the gas resources of the PNG highlands, Nelson said in the statement.

It would ensure the system was engineered from the outset to provide capacity and interconnectibility with those sources of gas which had been identified and to provide expansion capability to serve market growth and new supply sources, he said.
The pipeline would come ashore on Australia's Cape York Peninsula and will be routed to the north Queensland industrial centre and port of Townsville, Nelson said.

Kutubu participants are Oil Search with 7.763 percent, Chevron Niugini Pty Ltd 19.375 percent, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd unit BHP Petroleum (PNG) Inc 9.688 percent, BP Australia Ltd 19.375 percent, Ampolex 16.455 percent, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd affiliate JPP 4.844 percent, and the PNG government 22.50 percent.
